title: Elder Kuṭivihāri (2): This hut is old. You want a new hut. Give up wanting a hut; a new hut brings new suffering. Know this,…
content:
Elder Kuṭivihāri (2):

This hut is old. You want a new hut.
Give up wanting a hut; a new hut brings new suffering.
Know this, O bhikkhu!

title: Bhikkhus, what is the course of practice that is painful with slow direct knowledge? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the foul on the body,…
content: Bhikkhus, what is the course of practice that is painful with slow direct knowledge? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the foul on the body, with perception of disgust for food, with perception of non-delight in the entire world, contemplating impermanence in all formations, and the perception of death is well established internally. He lives depending on the five learner's powers, that is, the power of faith, the power of conscience, the power of fear of wrongdoing, the power of energy, the power of wisdom. For him, these five faculties appear very soft: the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom. Because these five faculties appear very soft, he attains the immediate concentration for the destruction of the taints slowly. This, bhikkhus, is called the course of practice that is painful with slow direct knowledge.

title: Brahmā, bhikkhus, is a designation for mother and father; the ancient teachers, bhikkhus, is a designation for mother and father; the devas of old, bhikkhus,…
content: Brahmā, bhikkhus, is a designation for mother and father; the ancient teachers, bhikkhus, is a designation for mother and father; the devas of old, bhikkhus, is a designation for mother and father; worthy of offerings and reverence, bhikkhus, is a designation for mother and father. Why is that? Because, bhikkhus, mother and father have done much for their children: they nourish them, bring them up, and introduce them to this world.

title: Brahmin, the Blessed One, the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, has laid down the training rules, has proclaimed the Pātimokkha for…
content: Brahmin, the Blessed One, the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, has laid down the training rules, has proclaimed the Pātimokkha for the bhikkhus. On Uposatha days we reside in the same village, all of us gather together in one place; having assembled, we ask about what has happened to each one. If, while thus questioning, a bhikkhu has committed an offense, a breach of the precepts, we make him act according to the Dhamma, according to the instruction. Truly, it is not the venerable ones who rule over us; it is the Dhamma that rules over us.

title: Elder Nun Mittā: On the fourteenth, the fifteenth, On the eighth of each half-month, On the special fast-day of the lunar fortnight, I observed the…
content:
Elder Nun Mittā:

On the fourteenth, the fifteenth,
On the eighth of each half-month,
On the special fast-day of the lunar fortnight,
I observed the eight precepts.

I kept the uposatha observance,
Making the devas rejoice.
Eating one meal a day,
Shaven-headed, wearing the great robe,
I do not long for the heavenly realm,
I subdue the suffering of the mind.

title: And, bhikkhus, a true person reflects: 'It is not because of being a forest-dweller that the states of greed come to be abandoned, or the…
content: And, bhikkhus, a true person reflects: 'It is not because of being a forest-dweller that the states of greed come to be abandoned, or the states of hatred, or the states of delusion. If a person who has gone forth is not a forest-dweller, yet practices in accordance with the Dhamma and in conformity with the Dhamma, practices rightly, practices in conformity with the Dhamma, then he is honored and praised here.' Having taken the path as the essential, he does not praise himself or disparage others because of his own being a forest-dweller. Thus, bhikkhus, is the true person's quality.

title: Fear, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. Suffering, bhikkhus, is a companion of sensual pleasures. Illness, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. A…
content: Fear, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. Suffering, bhikkhus, is a companion of sensual pleasures. Illness, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. A boil, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. Clinging, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. A swamp, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. And, bhikkhus, why is fear a designation for sensual pleasures? Bhikkhus, being infatuated by sensual desire, bound by sensual desire, one does not escape from fear in this very life, nor does one escape from fear in the hereafter. Therefore, fear is a designation for sensual pleasures.

title: Bhikkhus, I sought the gratification in the world. Whatever gratification there is in the world, I found it. To whatever extent gratification exists in the…
content: Bhikkhus, I sought the gratification in the world. Whatever gratification there is in the world, I found it. To whatever extent gratification exists in the world, I have seen it well with wisdom. Bhikkhus, I sought the danger in the world. Whatever danger there is in the world, I found it. To whatever extent danger exists in the world, I have seen it well with wisdom. Bhikkhus, I sought the escape from the world. Whatever escape there is from the world, I found it. To whatever extent escape exists from the world, I have seen it well with wisdom.

title: Bhikkhus, it is through attachment that one is not liberated. Through attachment to form, bhikkhus, consciousness, having a foothold, becomes established. With form as object,…
content: Bhikkhus, it is through attachment that one is not liberated. Through attachment to form, bhikkhus, consciousness, having a foothold, becomes established. With form as object, with form as support, seeking delight, it comes to growth, increase, and expansion. Through attachment to feeling ... through attachment to perception ... through attachment to formations, bhikkhus, consciousness, having a foothold, becomes established. With formations as object, with formations as support, seeking delight, it comes to growth, increase, and expansion. Bhikkhus, one who says: 'Apart from form, apart from feeling, apart from perception, apart from formations, I will describe the coming and going, the passing away and arising, the growth, increase, and expansion of consciousness' — that is impossible. Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu has abandoned lust for the form element, with the abandonment of lust, the basis is cut off, and the support of consciousness does not exist. Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu has abandoned lust for the feeling element ... for the perception element ... for the formation element ... Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu has abandoned lust for the consciousness element, with the abandonment of lust, the basis is cut off, and the support of consciousness does not exist. Without that support, consciousness does not grow, does not form, is liberated. Through liberation, it is steady. Through steadiness, it is content. Through contentment, it is not distressed. Not distressed, he personally attains Nibbāna. He understands: 'Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no further existence after this life.'

title: In whatever families, bhikkhus, the children at home honor their mother and father, those families are considered equal to Brahmā. In whatever families, bhikkhus, the…
content: In whatever families, bhikkhus, the children at home honor their mother and father, those families are considered equal to Brahmā. In whatever families, bhikkhus, the children at home honor their mother and father, those families are considered like the ancient teachers. In whatever families, bhikkhus, the children at home honor their mother and father, those families are considered worthy of offerings.
